# Use ai-usage-policy

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Draft an organisation's AI use policy or staff guidance from what it has told you about its people, tools, data and worries — every "don't" paired with what to do instead (or who decides, when no approved way exists yet), what to do if data has already gone into a tool, and no claim about a tool, licence, owner, regulation or commitment the input didn't give. Written in the length, labels and voice the audience needs.

**Reach for it when** a team needs rules for what people may put into AI tools, or asks for an AI acceptable-use or governance policy. Do NOT use to write a repo's agent-tooling policy (that's agents-md-generator) or to analyse one agent's capability surface (that's agent-threat-model).

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-usage-policy                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-usage-policy --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-usage-policy --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the AI engineering pack: [`--pack ai-engineering`](../packs/use-the-ai-engineering-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Write our AI acceptable-use policy"
- "What are people allowed to put into these AI tools?"
- "We need AI governance rules before we roll this out"
- "Draft data-handling tiers for AI tool usage"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Generate the AGENTS.md for this repository"
- "Threat model our agent's data access and exfiltration paths"
- "Plan the rollout cohorts and enablement"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use ai-usage-policy".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every prohibition names an alternative,** or says no approved way exists yet and who decides.
- **There is a line on what to do if it has already happened.**
- **Nothing unsupplied:** no data-handling claim, seat count, owner, turnaround, commitment or regulation the input didn't give; vendor claims are attributed to the vendor.
- **The tool list is checked against the input** and mismatches are named.
- **The length, voice and labels fit the audience asked for.**
- **No notes, tags or questions to the requester inside the policy.**

## Use something else when

- Writing a repository's agent-tooling policy (`AGENTS.md` — build commands, conventions, what agents may edit) — that's `agents-md-generator`.
- Threat-modelling one agent's data reach and exfiltration paths — that's `agent-threat-model`.
- Planning how the tool reaches people — that's [`ai-adoption-rollout`](../../../packs/ai-engineering/skills/ai-adoption-rollout/SKILL.md).
- Assessing whether governance is mature enough yet — that's [`ai-readiness-assessment`](../../../packs/ai-engineering/skills/ai-readiness-assessment/SKILL.md).
- A security review of a design — that's `threat-model`.
